patterns: What are Saturn's rings made of?
responses: Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock, from tiny grains to chunks as big as houses.
Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick clouds trap heat, making it hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the sun.
Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system.
The sun is the closest star. After the sun, the nearest is Proxima Centauri, about 4.2 light years away.
A light year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
The International Space Station is a science lab orbiting Earth about every 90 minutes, where astronauts live and do experiments.

patterns: How do I become an astronaut?
responses: Astronauts usually study science, engineering, or medicine, get lots of experience, stay very fit, and train for years in things like spacewalks and survival.
A comet is a ball of ice and dust that grows a glowing tail near the sun. A shooting star is a tiny space rock burning up in our atmosphere.

patterns: Is there life on other planets?
responses: No one has found alien life yet. Scientists are searching, especially on Mars and moons like Europa and Enceladus that may have water.
The Big Bang is the idea that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago from an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since.
A solar eclipse is when the moon passes between Earth and the sun. A lunar eclipse is when Earth's shadow falls on the moon.
Rainforests are warm, wet forests full of life. They are home to about half of the world's plant and animal species and help clean the air.
The biggest desert is Antarctica, because a desert means very little rain or snow. The biggest hot desert is the Sahara.
Elephants are the largest land animals. They are very smart, have great memories, and live in close family groups.
Dolphins are smart, playful mammals that breathe air. They talk to each other with clicks and whistles.

patterns: Why can owls turn their heads?
responses: Owls are night hunters with amazing hearing. They can turn their heads about 270 degrees because their eyes can't move in their sockets.
A caterpillar forms a chrysalis, and inside, its body completely rebuilds into a butterfly. That change is called metamorphosis.
Frogs are amphibians. They start life as tadpoles in water, then grow legs and lungs so they can live on land too.
Turtles have shells that are part of their skeleton. Some tortoises can live more than 100 years.
Snakes are reptiles with no legs. Most snakes are not venomous, and they smell with their tongues.

patterns: How fast can a horse run?
responses: Horses are strong, fast animals that have worked with people for thousands of years. They can gallop around 50 kilometers per hour.
Spiders are not insects. They are arachnids with eight legs, while insects have six. Most spiders are harmless and eat pests.
Ants live in big colonies with a queen. They can carry many times their own body weight.
Yes. Humpback whales sing long, complex songs that can travel for miles underwater.
Koalas aren't bears. They are marsupials from Australia that carry babies in a pouch and eat eucalyptus leaves.
